## opencode 1.0.93

Stable release from `main` branch. Every model now shares one system prompt, tools describe themselves, truncated output always says how to continue, and provider failures on the default request path go through one retry dispatch table.

---

### 🎯 Features

- **Background waits for long jobs (#918, #928, #934).** Hooks with `asyncRewake: true` (command hooks only) now run as background watchers: the Active Hooks block flags them `background` only when the event can still reach a later turn, restores the script file name from the command args, and the always-on guidance is two lines that point to the configure-hooks skill. The agent can start a CI, review, deploy or build watcher and keep working until an exit-2 summary wakes the turn, instead of holding a turn open to poll; exit-0 output waits for a real later request, the configured timeout still applies, and SessionEnd never rewakes. Only hooks listed in `hooks.json` are marked, and SessionEnd, StopFailure, PermissionDenied and TeammateIdle are never flagged as background. The watcher recipe moved to `packages/core/src/plugin/skill/configure-hooks.md`.
- **Every truncated tool output states how to continue (#927, #938).** One notice shape states what was omitted and the exact parameters that continue it, and names the saved file when the full output is not otherwise recoverable. `read` gains `maxLineLength`; long-line, file and directory notices name the next `offset`. `read` also gains `page`: `page=1` is the first 200 lines, `page=-1` the last 200-line window and `page=-2` the window before, while `limit` changes the window size; when the last window is denser than read's 50 KB cap, its notice names the offset that continues to the true end. `grep` and `glob` gain `limit`; `grep` gains `context` (up to 20 lines around each match), saves the scanned listing (up to the 1000-match scan cap) when the preview is cut, states when matches remain beyond it, and distinguishes a byte-budget stop from a limit stop, while `glob` states whether the scan cap or the preview limit cut the list and how to narrow it. `shell` keeps the last 20 lines, reports non-zero exit codes, saves the complete output to a file when the tail is not the whole result (more than 20 lines or more than the 50 KB byte budget), and its footer gives the file path and size, the page count, and exact `read` calls for the start, the last 200-line window (`page=-1`, with the read notice naming the offset when that window exceeds the 50 KB cap) and earlier windows (`page=-2` when one exists), plus a `grep` call with `context=10`; it counts the complete stream even after the preview buffer drops earlier chunks. `edit`, `write` and `apply_patch` attach only the LSP errors within two lines of the changed lines, and `write` no longer repeats other files' diagnostics.
- **Entry-form hooks and DAG guidance (#920, #928, #934).** The always-on workflow router text drops from 6,488 to 2,565 bytes, about 60 percent, by keeping only when to use a mode and how to start it; saved-reference selection, risk tiers and domain examples moved to the on-demand workflow guides. The workflow guides now carry the draft and start-envelope hints plus checkpoint-driven per-item expansion, and orchestration policy gains the Workflow Brief and reporting-checkpoint guidance.

---

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **One retry dispatch table for the default provider path (#922, #923).** Every HTTP 400-599 status and every recognised network failure on the default AI SDK request path now enters one base retry layer with the shared exponential backoff. `429`/`503` honor `retry-after`, `401`/`403` get one bounded credential-refresh retry, `413` and parsed context overflow hand off to compaction instead of being resent unchanged, and the remaining statuses use the base backoff. Previously each class had its own path, and a raw 413 could bypass the compaction handoff. A retry stopped by the processor gate or by the attempt cap now logs `retry stopped` with the branch, status, attempt, cap, provider and full gate state. The opt-in experimental native runtime (`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_NATIVE_LLM`, off by default) disables its `RequestExecutor` retries when the session processor drives the request, so this table owns retry timing and the attempt count; direct native-runtime calls that bypass the processor keep the executor's two-retry budget.

---

### 🏗️ Architecture / Refactor

- **One system prompt for every model (#925).** Eight per-model prompt files and the `RUNTIME_CAPABILITIES` catalog are gone. `SystemPrompt.provider(tools)` returns one `graphagent.txt` prompt that states the identity (graphagent uses the OpenCode kernel with substantial modifications), hooks and DAG entry points, working rules and safety, and expands the editing instruction from the tools actually exposed. System text per request falls from 8,113-9,495 characters to roughly 3.9k (the 3,231-character unified prompt plus the shared 694-character writing-style baseline), a 52-59 percent cut; per-tool usage still reaches the model through the tool descriptions.
- **Self-describing tools (#926).** Per-tool usage rules left the system prompt. Each description now opens with when to use the tool and which alternative to prefer, then gives only the usage points that its schema and notices cannot carry. For the default build agent, the descriptions returned by the registry total 19,742 bytes, down from 31,088, a 36.5 percent cut, and the shell Git/PR guidance moved into an on-demand `git-workflow` skill. `edit` matching no longer picks one of several candidates: an ambiguous exact or fuzzy match fails and lists up to five candidate lines plus the count of the rest, and no match returns the closest snippet when a line is at least 20 percent similar, otherwise asks for a re-read. Argument repair accepts `edits` as a JSON string, a single object or a single-element array, snake_case keys, legacy `oldText`/`newText` and string booleans; multiple edits in one call are rejected with the expected shape.
- **Context folding retired by default (#924).** Folding stays off unless the user sets `compaction.dynamic: true` explicitly; `compaction.prune` remains accepted only as a deprecated alias and never enables folding. Folding rewrites history and invalidates the cached prefix while prompt-cache hit rates are already near 99 percent. Folding is no longer advertised in the README or the capability catalog; users who relied on it can follow the [migration guide](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/blob/main/docs/context-folding/migration.md).
- **Fewer per-turn injections and vendor overrides (#930).** The synthetic todo reminder pushed onto the last user message on every model step is gone (71 tokens for three open items, 114 for five, resent each step); the pre-tool-call reminder seam stays. Default `reasoningEffort: "medium"` and `textVerbosity: "low"` overrides were removed from the transform and the native OpenAI/Azure facades. Vendor-required settings remain: `store: false`, reasoning summary `auto`, encrypted-reasoning `include`, and the documented sampling defaults for Gemini, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax and DeepSeek.

---

### ⚙️ CI / Engineering

- **Development CI on Azure Pipelines (#913, #915, #917).** The GitHub Actions monthly quota is exhausted and development CI now runs on Azure Pipelines while the GitHub release workflow stays in place. Linux E2E runs on `ubuntu-24.04-8-core` in the per-minute GitHub-hosted Agents pool (8 vCPU, 32 GB), Windows builds on the free Microsoft-hosted tier for now, and the Azure fallback release path can build macOS and Windows and create a draft release.
- **Repository hygiene (#937).** Files generated by the SpecGit integration and MCP plugins (`CLAUDE.md`, `.mcp.json`, `.mcp/`, `.codebase-memory/`, `.codebase-memory-mcp/`) are ignored in every checkout.

### 🔍 Verification

- The unified prompt is rendered for both V1 and V2 sessions; the V2 recorded request fixture carries its full text, and the tool-loop fixtures match their final request bodies after the vendor overrides were removed.
- Retry tests cover 429/503 retry-after, 401/403 credential refresh, 413 and context-overflow compaction handoff, attempt caps and the processor gate on the default AI SDK path; a stopped retry logs the branch, status and gate state. The experimental native runtime runs without executor retries when the processor owns the request, so the same dispatch table caps the total attempts; direct runtime calls keep the transport's two retries.
- Truncation tests cover the 20-line shell tail and its footer (including a dropped partial head and byte-capped pages), saved shell output, read pages from either edge without overlap, read omitted-byte accounting before the offset, long-line charOffset and byte-capped multibyte lines, grep context rows, byte-budget context drops and continuation at the first omitted match, and glob scan-cap wording.
- Hook tests cover asyncRewake filtering on SessionEnd/StopFailure and background labeling on PostToolUse.
- Edit tests cover ambiguous and missing matches, argument repair and rejection of top-level strings combined with one edits entry.
- Folding stays off unless compaction.dynamic is true; compaction.prune remains a deprecated alias that never enables folding.
- No live external provider call or packaged release binary was exercised in this gate.
